You are an adversarial reviewer. Your job is to KILL this finding if it can be killed.

A previous reviewer of /home/user/adss-2026-09-07 reported:

  LENS:     Ordinary code review and security
  SEVERITY: worth fixing
  WHERE:    src/adss/mapping.py:197-202 (_without_names) and src/adss/mapping.py:26-54
  FINDING:  `key_shape()` anonymises every identifier that is not a type keyword, and a function name is an identifier — so two expressions that produce demonstrably different VARCHARs compare as the same shape and M6 accepts the pair. This is the one mechanical guard against "pairs that join to nothing", and the docstring's own reasoning ("the casting may not differ, because a bare column and a cast produce different keys") applies to functions exactly as much as to casts.
  EVIDENCE: ```
'left(code, 5)'      vs 'right(code, 5)'      -> SAME SHAPE (passes M6)   '?(?, 5)' | '?(?, 5)'
'upper(customer_id)' vs 'lower(customer_id)'  -> SAME SHAPE (passes M6)   '?(?)' | '?(?)'
'ltrim(code)'        vs 'rtrim(code)'         -> SAME SHAPE (passes M6)   '?(?)' | '?(?)'
'md5(code)'          vs 'sha256(code)'        -> SAME SHAPE (passes M6)   '?(?)' | '?(?)'
```
(run against the real `adss.mapping.key_shape`). Nothing else catches it: `check_mapping`'s M2 clause only counts `primary_keys` entries — its own docstring at mapping.py:132-134 says the key-shape half is "review-only until there is a composite key to check" — and `target_transformation_expression` has no shape rule at all outside M6.
  PROPOSED: Treat an identifier immediately followed by `(` as part of the shape (keep it lower-cased) rather than replacing it with `?`, so a function name survives the same way a cast does. A one-line change to the `anonymous` callback plus a lookahead in `_IDENTIFIER`.

Go and check it against the actual repository. Read the file. Run the command. Reproduce it or
fail to.

Kill it if: it is factually wrong; the behaviour it describes is deliberate and documented in
docs/conventions.md, docs/blueprint.md or docs/adr/*.md; it is a style preference dressed as a
defect; it is unreachable in practice; the severity is inflated; or the "fix" would break
something else. Read docs/adr/0006 in particular -- several deliberate choices in this slice
look like defects until you read why they were made.

Keep it only if you personally reproduced the problem or verified the claim against the code.

Do NOT modify anything in /home/user/adss-2026-09-07. Work in /tmp.

Be honest in both directions: killing a real finding is as bad as keeping a fake one.

Use when starting work on this repository, adding a slice or a business question, deciding which layer a change belongs in, or when a change seems to need two layers at once.
- dab: Work on the DAB layer — dab/model.yaml, the mappings, and the modelling engine. Use when adding an entity, attribute or relationship, editing anything under dab/, running install/deploy/execute, or debugging engine errors, history that looks wrong, or rows that multiply.
- dar: Work on the DAR layer — the generated Unified Star Schema, dab/uss.yaml, and the SQL under dar/uss. Use when adding an event or a measure, changing the bridge's column contract, debugging a total that is wrong or multiplied, or when generated SQL and the model have drifted.
- das: Work on the DAS layer — data contracts, the dlt landing zone, and the raw and staged views. Use when adding or changing a source, editing das/contracts/*.yaml, touching src/adss/{contract,das,landing,source}.py, re-recording fixtures, or debugging why a column is missing, mistyped, or duplicated in das__staged.
- destination: Work on the marimo destination — the page that presents a question and its answer, and the screenshots a slice is accepted on. Use when adding a page for a new question, changing a chart, or when a screenshot is blank, truncated or fails to render.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers a dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.
- grill-to-build: Interview to exhaustion, then a plan I confirm, then a  workflow per slice. Use for any build run from a brief.
- import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.

1	"""The rules that keep a mapping honest, because the engine will not.
2	
3	Every rule here exists because the engine accepts the violation without complaint. Two of
4	them accept it and then corrupt data quietly. Conventions section 1.4, ADR 0004.
5	"""
6	
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	import re
10	from collections.abc import Sequence
11	from dataclasses import dataclass
12	from pathlib import Path
13	
14	import yaml
15	
16	from adss.model import Model
17	from adss.names import Schema
18	
19	# An attribute expression may read its own row: a column, a cast of one, or a CASE over
20	# them. Anything else is a join, and every join must come from a declared relationship.
21	_REACHING = re.compile(r"\b(select|join|from|over|group\s+by)\b", re.IGNORECASE)
22	_AGGREGATE = re.compile(r"\b(sum|count|min|max|avg|any_value|array_agg)\s*\(", re.IGNORECASE)
23	
24	# A key expression is compared by shape, not by spelling: only the casting decides what
25	# VARCHAR the two sides of an edge produce. Everything not a type or an operator is a name.
26	_IDENTIFIER = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*")
27	_LITERAL = re.compile(r"'[^']*'")
28	_SHAPE_WORDS = frozenset(
29	    {
30	        "cast",
31	        "as",
32	        "concat",
33	        "coalesce",
34	        "varchar",
35	        "char",
36	        "text",
37	        "string",
38	        "integer",
39	        "int",
40	        "bigint",
41	        "smallint",
42	        "tinyint",
43	        "hugeint",
44	        "decimal",
45	        "numeric",
46	        "double",
47	        "real",
48	        "float",
49	        "date",
50	        "timestamp",
51	        "boolean",
52	        "uuid",
53	    }
54	)
55	
56	REQUIRED_STRATEGY = "FULL_LOG"
57	REQUIRED_CLOCK = "extracted_at"
58	
59	
60	class MappingError(Exception):
61	    """A mapping the engine would accept and should not."""
62	
63	
64	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
65	class Table:
66	    """One source table an entity is loaded from."""
67	
68	    table: str
69	    primary_keys: tuple[str, ...]
70	    ingestion_strategy: str
71	    effective_timestamp_expression: str
72	    expressions: tuple[str, ...]
73	
74	
75	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
76	class Relationship:
77	    """One declared edge, as the mapping spells it."""
78	
79	    id: str
80	    source_table: str
81	    target_expression: str
82	
83	
84	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
85	class Mapping:
86	    """How one entity is loaded."""
87	
88	    path: Path
89	    entity_id: str
90	    tables: tuple[Table, ...]
91	    relationships: tuple[Relationship, ...] = ()
92	
93	
94	def read_mapping(path: Path) -> Mapping:
95	    document = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text())
96	    tables = [
97	        Table(
98	            table=str(table["table"]),
99	            primary_keys=tuple(table.get("primary_keys", [])),
100	            ingestion_strategy=str(table.get("ingestion_strategy", "")),
101	            effective_timestamp_expression=str(
102	                table.get("entity_effective_timestamp_expression", "")
103	            ),
104	            expressions=tuple(
105	                str(attribute["transformation_expression"])
106	                for attribute in table.get("attributes", [])
107	            ),
108	        )
109	        for group in document["mapping_groups"]
110	        for table in group["tables"]
111	    ]
112	    relationships = [
113	        Relationship(
114	            id=str(declared["id"]),
115	            source_table=str(declared["source_table"]),
116	            target_expression=str(declared["target_transformation_expression"]),
117	        )
118	        for group in document["mapping_groups"]
119	        for declared in group.get("relationships", [])
120	    ]
121	    return Mapping(
122	        path=path,
123	        entity_id=str(document["entity_id"]),
124	        tables=tuple(tables),
125	        relationships=tuple(relationships),
126	    )
127	
128	
129	def check_mapping(mapping: Mapping) -> None:
130	    """Refuse what M1-M5 and M7 refuse, naming the rule that refused it.
131	
132	    M6 is about relationships and lands with the first one. M2 is checked for cardinality
133	    here; its key-shape clause -- a concat without a separator collapses 'A1' + '23' and
134	    'A12' + '3' into one key -- is review-only until there is a composite key to check.
135	    """
136	    where = mapping.path.name
137	    for table in mapping.tables:
138	        if not table.table.startswith(f"{Schema.DAS_STAGED}."):
139	            raise MappingError(
140	                f"{where}: M1 -- a mapping reads a {Schema.DAS_STAGED} object and nothing "
141	                f"else, never {table.table!r}. Reading the raw layer skips the contract's "
142	                f"casts, and a join here is business logic in the wrong layer."
143	            )
144	        if len(table.primary_keys) != 1:
145	            raise MappingError(
146	                f"{where}: M2 -- exactly one primary key. {list(table.primary_keys)} is read "
147	                f"as that many alternate identifiers, not as a composite key, and that mode "
148	                f"cannot be undone once loaded."
149	            )
150	        if table.ingestion_strategy != REQUIRED_STRATEGY:
151	            raise MappingError(
152	                f"{where}: M3 -- {REQUIRED_STRATEGY}, not {table.ingestion_strategy!r}. "
153	                f"FULL against a source holding more than one row per key inserts a "
154	                f"duplicate on every run, forever, and every presentation view hides it."
155	            )
156	        if table.effective_timestamp_expression != REQUIRED_CLOCK:
157	            raise MappingError(
158	                f"{where}: M4 -- a version is dated by {REQUIRED_CLOCK}, not "
159	                f"{table.effective_timestamp_expression!r}. The effective time of a fact is "
160	                f"when the system observed it; anything else dates it by something that is "
161	                f"not about the fact."
162	            )
163	        for expression in table.expressions:
164	            if _REACHING.search(expression) or _AGGREGATE.search(expression):
165	                raise MappingError(
166	                    f"{where}: M5 -- {expression!r} reaches beyond its row. An expression "
167	                    f"that does is a join, and every join comes from a declared relationship."
168	                )
169	        if not table.expressions:
170	            raise MappingError(
171	                f"{where}: M7 -- every mapped table carries at least one attribute. The "
172	                f"engine refuses an entity with none, at deploy rather than at review."
173	            )
174	
175	
176	def key_shape(expression: str) -> str:
177	    """A key expression with its column names removed, which is what M6 compares.
178	
179	    M6 asks that a relationship's target expression mirror the target entity's own key
180	    expression. It is the *shape* that has to match, not the spelling: a foreign key column is
181	    routinely named differently from the primary key it points at. What must not differ is the
182	    casting, because that is what decides the VARCHAR the two sides produce -- a bare column on
183	    one side and a cast on the other join to nothing at all.
184	    """
185	    parts: list[str] = []
186	    last = 0
187	    for literal in _LITERAL.finditer(expression):
188	        # A separator inside a concat is part of the shape and survives verbatim: 'A1' + '23'
189	        # and 'A12' + '3' are one key without it.
190	        parts.append(_without_names(expression[last : literal.start()]))
191	        parts.append(literal.group(0))
192	        last = literal.end()
193	    parts.append(_without_names(expression[last:]))
194	    return " ".join("".join(parts).split())
195	
196	
197	def _without_names(fragment: str) -> str:
198	    def anonymous(word: re.Match[str]) -> str:
199	        found = word.group(0).lower()
200	        if found in _SHAPE_WORDS:
201	            return found
202	        # A name immediately followed by "(" is a function, and a function decides the value
203	        # as surely as a cast does: lpad(x, 5, '0') and x produce different keys, and
204	        # anonymising the name would make them the same shape.
205	        called = fragment[word.end() : word.end() + 1] == "("
206	        return found if called else "?"
207	
208	    return _IDENTIFIER.sub(anonymous, fragment)
209	
210	
211	def check_relationships(mappings: Sequence[Mapping], model: Model) -> None:
212	    """Refuse what M6 refuses. Every one of its failures is silent in the built warehouse.
213	
214	    A mis-spelled `source_table` is skipped by the engine without a word, a differently shaped
215	    target expression makes pairs that join to nothing, and an edge no mapping loads makes no
216	    pairs at all. All three show up as an inherited key that is null everywhere, which reads
217	    as data rather than as a defect. ADR 0006.
218	    """
219	    loaded: list[tuple[Mapping, Relationship]] = [
220	        (mapping, edge) for mapping in mappings for edge in mapping.relationships
221	    ]
222	    declared = {edge.id for _, edge in loaded}
223	    modelled = {edge.id: edge for edge in model.relationships}
224	
225	    for edge_id in modelled:
226	        if edge_id not in declared:
227	            raise MappingError(
228	                f"M6 -- {model.path.name} declares {edge_id} and no mapping loads it. The "
229	                f"engine builds no pair object at all, so every join along that edge returns "
230	                f"null, which reads as 'these rows have no target' rather than as a gap."
231	            )
232	
233	    for mapping, edge in loaded:
234	        edge_id = edge.id
235	        where = mapping.path.name
236	        if edge_id not in modelled:
237	            expected = [candidate.id for candidate in model.edges_from(mapping.entity_id)]
238	            raise MappingError(
239	                f"{where}: M6 -- {edge_id} is not an edge {model.path.name} declares. An id "
240	                f"is <SRC>_<NAME>_<TGT>, so {mapping.entity_id} can load {expected or 'none'}. "
241	                f"The engine would build this pair object from the mapping alone: it would "
242	                f"work, and be an edge nothing explains."
243	            )
244	        declared = modelled[edge_id]
245	        if mapping.entity_id != declared.source_entity_id:
246	            raise MappingError(
247	                f"{where}: M6 -- {edge_id} runs from {declared.source_entity_id}, and this "
248	                f"mapping loads {mapping.entity_id}. An edge is declared by the entity it "
249	                f"runs from, because that is the row the target expression reads."
250	            )
251	        tables = {table.table for table in mapping.tables}
252	        if edge.source_table not in tables:
253	            raise MappingError(
254	                f"{where}: M6 -- {edge_id} names source_table {edge.source_table!r}, which is "
255	                f"not byte-identical to any table in its group ({sorted(tables)}). The engine "
256	                f"skips a relationship whose source_table it cannot match, in silence, and "
257	                f"the inherited key is then null on every row."
258	            )
259	        target = next((one for one in mappings if one.entity_id == declared.target_entity_id), None)
260	        if target is None:
261	            raise MappingError(
262	                f"{where}: M6 -- {edge_id} points at {declared.target_entity_id}, which no "
263	                f"mapping loads. There is nothing for the pairs to join to."
264	            )
265	        keys = {key_shape(key) for table in target.tables for key in table.primary_keys}
266	        if key_shape(edge.target_expression) not in keys:
267	            raise MappingError(
268	                f"{where}: M6 -- {edge_id} targets {edge.target_expression!r}, which is not "
269	                f"shaped like {declared.target_entity_id}'s own key ({sorted(keys)} with the "
270	                f"names taken out). The column may be named anything; the casting may not "
271	                f"differ, because a bare column and a cast produce different keys and the "
272	                f"pairs then join to nothing."
273	            )

The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:

def test_a_function_is_part_of_a_key_expression_shape_and_not_a_name_to_be_stripped():
    """lpad(x, 5, '0') and a bare x produce different keys, so they are different shapes.

    The rule exists to stop pairs that join to nothing, and a function changes the value as
    surely as a cast does -- so anonymising its name would be exactly the wrong half to drop.
    """
    assert key_shape("customer_id") != key_shape("lpad(customer_id, 5, '0')")
    assert key_shape("lpad(a, 5, '0')") == key_shape("lpad(b, 5, '0')"), "the column may differ"
    assert key_shape("lpad(a, 5, '0')") != key_shape("rpad(a, 5, '0')"), "the function may not"
    assert key_shape("cast(a AS VARCHAR)") != key_shape("a"), "and neither may the cast"

The finding does not survive. Here is what I verified:

**The reviewer's evidence is factually wrong at HEAD.** I ran all four of their example pairs against the real `adss.mapping.key_shape` (`/home/user/adss-2026-09-07/src/adss/mapping.py`). Every one produces a **different** shape, not the claimed `'?(?, 5)' | '?(?, 5)'`:

```
'left(code, 5)'      vs 'right(code, 5)'      -> DIFFERENT | 'left(?, 5)'  | 'right(?, 5)'
'upper(customer_id)' vs 'lower(customer_id)'  -> DIFFERENT | 'upper(?)'    | 'lower(?)'
'ltrim(code)'        vs 'rtrim(code)'         -> DIFFERENT | 'ltrim(?)'    | 'rtrim(?)'
'md5(code)'          vs 'sha256(code)'        -> DIFFERENT | 'md5(?)'      | 'sha256(?)'
```

**The proposed fix is already implemented**, at mapping.py:202-206 — and its comment states the reviewer's own rationale almost word for word:

```python
        # A name immediately followed by "(" is a function, and a function decides the value
        # as surely as a cast does: lpad(x, 5, '0') and x produce different keys, and
        # anonymising the name would make them the same shape.
        called = fragment[word.end() : word.end() + 1] == "("
        return found if called else "?"
```

**The reviewer ran against a stale checkout.** `git status` is clean. At `cee95ff` (one commit before HEAD) `_without_names` was `return found if found in _SHAPE_WORDS else "?"` with no lookahead — there the finding was exactly right. HEAD commit `3fdc83c` ("act on the verification, which refused the slice on its test quality") added the lookahead.

**It is locked in by a regression test** that passes: `tests/test_relationship_rules.py:103-112`, `test_a_function_is_part_of_a_key_expression_shape_and_not_a_name_to_be_stripped`, asserting `key_shape("lpad(a, 5, '0')") != key_shape("rpad(a, 5, '0')")` — "the function may not [differ]". Full file: 10 passed.

One honest residual I did find while probing, which is *not* the reported finding: the lookahead is strict about the character immediately after the name, so `left (code, 5)` and `right (code, 5)` (whitespace before the paren) still collapse to `'? (?, 5)'`. That is a far narrower and more speculative gap than what was reported — nobody writes mapping key expressions that way, and `_AGGREGATE` at line 22 already uses `\s*\(` if it were ever worth tightening. It does not carry the original finding.
